html:
The Alaska Purchase was the sale of Russian America to the United States in 1867, for 7.2 million dollars, about two cents an acre. Secretary of State William Seward signed the treaty on 30 March 1867, and the flags were changed at Sitka on 18 October.

Russia sold because the colony lost money once the sea otters were hunted out, and after the Crimean War it feared it could not defend Alaska against Britain. Critics in the US mocked the deal as "Seward's Folly".

No Native nation was asked. Tlingit leaders said Russia had held only its forts, not their land. US rule brought new missions, salmon canneries and, with the Klondike gold rush of the late 1890s, a wave of prospectors. Alaska became a state in 1959. Oil found at Prudhoe Bay in 1968 led to the land claims settlement of 1971 with the Iñupiat, Yup'ik, Unangax̂ and other Alaska Natives.
